annotation.title_clean: Commission Staff Working Document: Subsidiarity Grid accompanying the Proposal for a Directive on adapting non-contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence
annotation.title_en: Commission Staff Working Document: Subsidiarity Grid accompanying the Proposal for a Directive on adapting non-contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Commission staff working document (subsidiarity grid) justifying the proposed AI Liability Directive: legal basis in Article 114 TFEU, shared competence, need for EU action against fragmentation, and proportionality of a minimum-harmonisation approach using disclosure of evidence and rebuttable causality presumptions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Legal basis is Article 114 TFEU; competence is shared.
National action alone would fragment 27 tort regimes and create legal uncertainty.
Directive uses minimum harmonisation: disclosure of information and rebuttable causality presumptions.
No reversal of burden of proof, to avoid hampering innovation.
Review clause to assess no-fault liability and mandatory insurance later.
